title: The best AI newsletters in 2026
summary: These AI newsletters will keep you informed without drowning you in information, whether you're a technical practitioner, business leader, or curious enthusiast.
body_markdown:
As a writer covering technology and AI, I spend plenty of time separating useful information from the hype. A good AI newsletter can help cut through that noise.


But the best newsletter depends on what you need. Someone making AI strategy decisions needs different coverage than someone looking for an[AI workflow](https://zapier.com/blog/ai-workflows/) they can try this afternoon.


To find the best AI newsletters, I started by researching my options and looking at what other folks were recommending. Then I signed up for anything that looked promising and worked my way through well over 100 emails over the course of two weeks. I checked how much each newsletter was actively publishing, compared their promised frequency with what arrived, and evaluated how useful the content was beyond the welcome gifts and promotional emails.


These nine stood out for different reasons. Whether you want technical context, an enjoyable news briefing, or practical help using AI, there's a starting point here for you.


## The best AI newsletters


### For decision-makers


-


The AI Optimist for AI strategy


-


Import AI for AI research and policy


-


The Batch for technical AI context


### For staying current


-


Superhuman for the best all-in-one daily AI newsletter


-


The Rundown AI for practical AI news


-


The Neuron for approachable AI news


### For practical application


-


Zapier for learning how to use AI at work


-


Ben's Bites for builders and tinkerers


-


100 school for learning by doing


## The best AI newsletter for AI strategy


### [The AI Optimist](https://what-now.beehiiv.com/)


Hugo Pickford-Wardle and his team created the AI Optimist. Hugo is an AI implementation advisor, educator, and founder with a background in guiding organizations through digital and AI-driven change.


The newsletter impressed me with its practical insights for business leaders. Each weekly issue sorts developments into three sections: Urgent Priorities, Strategic Opportunities, and Geek Out. The actionable framework helps leaders see what needs attention now, what belongs on the roadmap, and how AI developments could affect decisions such as which workflows to rethink or where to invest.


## The best AI newsletter for AI research and policy


### [Import AI](https://jack-clark.net/)


Import AI is authored by Jack Clark, former Policy Director at OpenAI and co-founder of Anthropic. He has extensive journalism experience (Bloomberg and The Register) and is a recognized voice on[AI governance](https://zapier.com/blog/ai-governance) , safety, and industry trends.


The newsletter takes a close look at the research, policy debates, and industry shifts shaping AI. Clark has been publishing it since 2016, so the newsletter has the benefit of long-term perspective as well as proximity to the field. It helps readers anticipate emerging capabilities and how they'll affect markets, explaining regulatory and ethical debates that influence AI adoption.


The writing is a bit dry for me, but it's filled with valuable nuggets about AI policy. Overall, it's best suited for those who want signal over noise on both technical and policy fronts.


## The best AI newsletter for technical AI context


### [The Batch](https://www.deeplearning.ai/the-batch/)


The Batch is for people who want to take a deeper look at the AI behind the news. Each newsletter spends more time with the story than a quick daily digest can. It digs into the models, builders, and systems behind major AI developments, then explains what they can do.


It's technical enough to help readers understand the substance behind major developments, but accessible enough for leaders and professionals who don't work in machine learning every day.


The Batch comes from DeepLearning.AI, founded by AI educator Andrew Ng, and includes a letter from him. But the real value is the newsletter itself: a clear, hype-resistant technical briefing that helps readers follow what is changing in AI and what those changes mean for your work.


## The best all-in-one daily AI newsletter


### [Superhuman](https://superhuman.ai/subscribe)


Superhuman delivers on a clear promise: "Get smarter about AI in 3 minutes a day." It's curated by Zain Kahn, known as an "AI tools guy" on social media.


In a few minutes, you can catch up on AI news, discover trending tools, pick up a prompt or tutorial, and find a practical idea for using AI at work. It's a useful choice for readers who want a reliable daily email that keeps them informed and gives them inspiration on how to use AI.


Superhuman also has a wider library of tool collections, tutorials, and prompt resources when a quick daily tip turns into a deeper rabbit hole.


Because the content is so broad, don't expect a deep dive into any particular topic with Superhuman. But it's a good option if you're looking to stay in touch with new updates and ideas.


## The best AI newsletter for practical AI news


### [The Rundown AI](https://www.therundown.ai/)


The Rundown AI was founded by Rowan Cheung, who built a reputation for no-nonsense daily AI updates. Thanks to its reliability and focus on practical applications instead of just news reporting, The Rundown AI rapidly grew to 2M+ subscribers and is trusted as a dependable daily business briefing that cuts through hype to deliver actionable intelligence.


Every weekday, The Rundown AI takes the biggest AI developments and adds the missing context.


I liked how it was skimmable without losing important elements. It does this by breaking up the latest developments into multiple sections for a quick read on what happened, the smaller details behind the story, and why it matters.


You can also find a few tidbits on the practical side of AI. The newsletter shares workflows the community is working on and also some trending tools to check out. Overall, it's a good fit for readers who want help connecting industry developments to ways they can use AI.


## The best AI newsletter for approachable AI news


### [The Neuron](https://www.theneurondaily.com/subscribe)


The Neuron takes AI seriously without taking itself too seriously. Its casual, playful personality makes it easier to read without feeling like you're trying to understand an industry report.


The newsletter packages AI news and useful tools into a five-minute read with a focus on developments that matter for your work. The lighter delivery makes it a good fit if you need to stay current but don't find the topic endlessly fascinating.


My signup experience even included an AI Cat Personality Quiz (I'm an Agile Housecat, thanks for asking). That whimsical streak makes the newsletter feel like something written for humans. And if daily emails are too much, you can switch to weekly.


## The best AI newsletter for learning how to use AI at work


### [Zapier blog newsletter](https://zapier.com/l/blog-subscribe)


[Zapier](https://zapier.com/) 's blog newsletter isn't exclusively about AI, but given how deeply AI now runs through Zapier's product and content, it's one of the most useful practical AI resources in circulation. Each email highlights in-depth guides, tutorials, and case studies showing how AI and automation can safely streamline your daily work.


Unlike news-heavy digests, the Zapier newsletter takes a show-don't-tell approach. Articles often feature AI and automation workflows you can copy directly into your own setup, tool comparisons and reviews to help you decide where AI adds the most value, and hands-on tutorials for integrating AI into everyday apps like Slack, Google Docs, and Airtable. The blog also covers[Zapier MCP](https://zapier.com/blog/zapier-mcp-guide/) , which lets you take action across 9,000+


apps straight from AI tools like Claude and ChatGPT—with tutorials on setting it up and putting it to work.


With millions of users already building automations through Zapier, the newsletter's angle is uniquely grounded in real-world AI productivity. The Zapier newsletter is an ideal choice for professionals seeking actionable guidance on securely integrating AI into their existing workflows, rather than abstract insights or speculative predictions.


## The best AI newsletter for builders and tinkerers


### [Ben's Bites](https://www.bensbites.com/)


Founded by Ben Tossell, founder of Makerpad (acquired by Zapier in 2021), Ben's Bites has attracted 170,000+ subscribers across tech, business, and startup circles. Ben's background combines product development, tech community leadership, and hands-on experimentation, making for insightful commentary in the realm of AI technology.


Ben's Bites is like peeking over the shoulder of someone building cool things with AI. Ben shares what he's trying and learning, alongside AI news and tool recommendations. Not every issue walks through one of his experiments, but his personal observations give the coverage a builder's perspective.


Alongside major headlines, you'll find links to agent tools, coding resources, and projects other people are making. It's a good fit if you want to follow AI developments with an eye toward what you could build—not just what companies are announcing.


The newsletter has both free and paid options. A key perk of the paid subscription is access to the builder community, where you can connect with others experimenting with AI. Start with the free version if you want to explore what people are making before committing to a subscription.


## The best AI newsletter for learning by doing


### [100 school](https://www.100school.com/)


You can use AI every day and still feel like you're winging it. 100 School meets you there and shares small experiments that help you get better at your work.


Instead of giving you another tool to bookmark, 100 School helps you find an approach worth trying and adapt it to your own tasks. The goal is to move beyond a good result in one chat toward something you'll actually use again.


I liked that it showed practical examples followed by guidance you can put to use. A workflow breakdown might come with a copyable prompt, while a hands-on experiment leads into related tutorials. That combination gives you enough context to understand the approach and somewhere to start testing it yourself.


It's a good fit if you've had useful moments with AI but haven't quite figured out how to repeat them.


## Which AI newsletter should you subscribe to?


You don't want to sign up for newsletters that end up collecting dust in your inbox. Think about what you need from AI right now: getting advice on building workflows calls for a different newsletter than receiving timely updates on AI policy. My suggestion is to start with a few and unsubscribe from the ones you never get around to reading, adding in more as your specific tastes and needs develop.


If you're just getting started with AI, I'd recommend beginning with The Rundown AI for practical applications and Zapier for specific workflows you can implement.


One newsletter might be enough. A few might work better. Either way, the goal is to get useful AI coverage you have time to read. If a newsletter keeps going unopened or repeats what you're getting elsewhere, it's fine to unsubscribe. You don't need to replace it—just keep the ones that earn your attention.
